transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi Dr. Smith. I came in because... well, I just can't stop feeling like I'm a danger and a disappointment. I had this one near-miss at work, and it really just proves to me that I'm not meant to be a nurse. I just keep thinking that everyone would be better off without me.
Did you start feeling this way—like a danger and a disappointment—only after that near-miss at work, or had you been feeling this way for a while before that happened?

No, it was definitely before that. The near-miss just... made it harder to ignore, I guess. I've actually been feeling like this for about a year and two months now. It pretty much started right after I graduated high school, when I began taking college classes and doing full-time clinic work.

Over this past year and two months, would you say you've felt this way—down and feeling like a disappointment—nearly every day, or has it come and gone with periods where you felt more like your usual self?

It's been nearly every day. Most days I just wake up with this heavy, empty feeling right in my chest. It doesn't really leave. Even when I'm trying to act normal at the clinic, like when I'm smiling at my patients in Spanish and just doing my job, I feel like I'm barely holding myself together.
Over this same period, have you noticed a loss of interest or pleasure in things you used to enjoy, even outside of work?

Yeah, I have. I used to do a lot of things to clear my head after class—like jogging, knitting, cooking, or just reading a book. But now... I just come home and sit on my bed in my scrubs. I just can't make myself care about doing any of it anymore.

Before this current period started about a year and two months ago, had you ever gone through a distinct episode of feeling this depressed in the past, followed by a time when you felt back to your normal self?

No, this is the first time. Before I graduated, I felt pretty normal. I didn't have any times where I felt this down or empty like I do now. It really just started a year and two months ago and hasn't stopped.

During this past year and two months, have you noticed significant changes in your sleep or appetite—like sleeping much more or less than usual, or a big change in your eating—along with trouble concentrating?

My sleep has definitely been a problem. At night, I just... I lie there replaying patient charts and medication calculations in my head. I can't seem to turn it off. And when I do finally fall asleep, I always end up waking up way before my alarm. I wake up already exhausted, and usually just scared that I missed something important at work. I haven't really noticed a big change in my eating, though.
Have you noticed feeling unusually fatigued or low on energy nearly every day during this past year and two months, even when you haven't exerted yourself much?

Um, no, not really. I mean, I'm definitely exhausted from not sleeping well, like I just mentioned, and my shifts at the hospital take a lot out of me. But... I haven't really noticed feeling unusually low on energy out of nowhere, especially if I haven't been doing anything. It's mostly just the tiredness from work and the lack of sleep.
You mentioned feeling like everyone would be better off without you—have you had any specific thoughts of harming yourself or ending your life?

No, I don't have a specific plan to hurt myself or anything like that. But... I do keep having these thoughts. Like, I'll just think that it would be so much easier if I just didn't wake up in the morning. Or if I could just... disappear. That way I wouldn't be around to mess anything else up.

How much are these feelings and symptoms affecting your ability to function—are you still managing to get through your work shifts and daily responsibilities, or has it become very difficult to keep up with them?

It's... it's gotten pretty difficult, honestly. I've actually fallen behind in my nursing prerequisites because I just can't focus on the coursework. And at the clinic... I'm just so worried I'm going to make a mistake. I've been asking my coworkers to double-check things for me—things I used to do on my own with no problem. It's gotten to the point where I'm just really afraid to take on my normal responsibilities at work because I don't trust myself right now.

Have you ever experienced anything like hearing voices or having thoughts that others might see as unusual or not based in reality, such as being convinced you truly deserve punishment for something you didn't actually do?

No, I haven't experienced anything like that. I don't hear voices or see things that aren't there. And I don't think I deserve punishment for something I didn't do... I just feel guilty about the things I actually am messing up, like school and work. But no unusual thoughts or voices.
How often do these thoughts about not waking up or disappearing occur—are they occasional, or are you experiencing them frequently throughout the day?

Um, they happen pretty frequently. Like I mentioned earlier, I really don't have any actual plan to hurt myself or do anything drastic. But those thoughts... about how it would just be easier to not wake up, or wishing I could just disappear so I don't mess anything else up... they cross my mind a lot. Probably a few times a day, honestly.
Beyond work and school, how are these feelings affecting other areas of your life—like taking care of yourself at home, seeing friends or family, or managing daily tasks?

Um, I'm not really sure. I guess I haven't really noticed a huge change with that stuff. I mostly just go home and stay in my room. I haven't really been seeing friends or doing much with my family... I just don't have the energy to go out or socialize after dealing with the clinic and my classes. So I mostly just keep to myself right now.
